entities.title: zazzle git runs as its own process, not through zazzled
entities.summary: The invoker execs the zazzle-git binary beside itself for `zazzle git`, and zazzle-git execs git for anything it does not answer itself.
entities.context: Most zazzle commands are requests to the zazzled daemon, which answers over a socket. The commit flow and the editor need the caller's own terminal (/dev/tty in raw mode, signals, git hooks and signing that may ask the user), the caller's working directory and git's own exit status.
entities.decision: tool_binary maps `git` to zazzle-git, which exec_tool runs from the invoker's directory; zazzle-git replaces itself with `git ARGS` for forwarded commands and runs git commit attached to the terminal with no timeout.
entities.rationale: A process of its own keeps the terminal, streams, environment and exit status the caller's, with nothing resident, as for free-disk-space and fix-network.

entities.title: A modeless editor
entities.summary: Keys type text; every command is a Ctrl, Alt, function or navigation key, and Ctrl+S saves and Esc cancels in every view.
entities.context: The editor is git's editor for short texts: commit messages, pull request bodies, changelog entries and rebase todo lists.
entities.decision: No insert or command mode: Editor::handle handles Ctrl+S, Esc, help, Tab and find before any view's keys, and the editing view inserts every plain character.
entities.rationale: No key changes what the next key does, and the key bar always shows how to save and cancel.

entities.title: Tab and Shift+Tab switch views
entities.summary: Tab moves forward and Shift+Tab back through the views offered (editing, then Files or Rebase); the editor never inserts a tab character.
entities.context: The commit flow needs a second screen for choosing files and a todo list needs one for commands, and commit messages do not need tab characters.
entities.decision: Tab and BackTab are global keys handled by cycle_view; inside the find-and-replace bar they switch between the query and the replacement instead.
entities.rationale: One well-known key reaches the other view from anywhere, and the key bar names the view Tab goes to.

entities.title: Ctrl+M and Ctrl+H are not commands
entities.summary: Terminals send Ctrl+M as the same byte as Enter (CR) and Ctrl+H as Backspace (BS), so the decoder treats them as Enter and Backspace and no command uses them.
entities.context: Without the kitty keyboard protocol a program cannot tell Ctrl+M from Enter or Ctrl+H from Backspace.
entities.decision: decode_simple maps CR and LF to Enter and DEL and BS to Backspace; commands use other Ctrl letters (S, G, F, R, K, Z, Y, A, C, X, V).
entities.rationale: A binding on Ctrl+M or Ctrl+H would fire on every Enter or Backspace in most terminals.

entities.title: Double and triple arrow taps instead of Ctrl+arrows, Home and End
entities.summary: A double tap moves by a word (left, right) or a page (up, down), a triple tap to the line's edge or the text's start or end; there are no Ctrl+arrow, Home or End bindings.
entities.context: On macOS Ctrl+arrows switch desktops by default, and many Mac keyboards have no Home or End key.
entities.decision: Taps::press counts presses of the same arrow within 250 ms; edit_arrow and list_arrow move from where the first tap started; Key has no Home or End.
entities.rationale: The same movement works with the arrow keys alone on every keyboard and terminal.

entities.title: Agents compose without tools, from a prompt on stdin, in their own process group
entities.summary: The commit message agent gets everything it needs in the prompt and is run so that it cannot change files (no tools for claude, a read-only sandbox for codex, plan mode for gemini), and so that stopping it stops everything it started.
entities.context: The agent runs while the developer is in the editor, on their working tree, without anyone watching it; it only has to write a few lines of text, and it may be restarted many times as marks change.
entities.decision: The prompt (instructions, branch, recent subjects, changes) goes on stdin. claude runs with `-p --tools "" --no-session-persistence --effort`; codex with `exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral -c model_reasoning_effort=… -`; gemini with `--approval-mode plan -p …`. Each is spawned with process_group(0), and stopping it sends SIGKILL to the whole group.
entities.rationale: No file edits behind the developer's back, no saved sessions to clutter claude's or codex's history, no argument length limit for a large diff, and no orphaned helper processes when the agent is cancelled, restarted or times out.
